featured_reviews.name: Siddharth Shivram
featured_reviews.review_text:
Based on my experience on 10th May 2021:

Since this is a new centre for vaccination opened last Friday by the BMC, there is not much clarity/information available online. This centre is currently open for 18-44 age group, and primarily Covaxin (subject to availability). There is not much clarity about walk-ins, better to call and confirm as they were only accepting appointments via CoWIN when I visited. Location specified on Google Maps is accurate.

An extremely well-maintained, organized vaccination centre with professional service by the officials. There are 3-4 levels of screenings and procedures before you get vaccinated, which is managed brilliantly. Prefer a morning slot if possible, reach the centre by 8:30am. They allow entry in an orderly manner at sharp 9am if everything goes well.

First level: General health details. Please provide accurate answers to the questions about any health conditions, symptoms, etc.

Second level: This is where you receive your token/card from BMC with all your details, verified with your appointment online. They will also specify booth/token number. After this, proceed to the waiting zone, which has an LED indicator to show the current token ongoing.

Third level: Once your token number is displayed, proceed to your booth (there are 2 booths which function simultaneously) and wait for the previous person to vacate. Get vaccinated, follow all the necessary instructions specified by the vaccinating doctor, and proceed towards the observation zone.

Fourth level: Wait patiently for 30 minutes. Please do not insist to leave any earlier, just to make sure there are no side effects. Once your 30-minute cooldown is complete, you can show your token/card and collect your vaccination certificate.

The entire process, takes just about 30-40 minutes, thanks to the dedicated staff (this was specifically for the morning slot 9-11am, your experience may vary depending on the time of the day).
Kindly co-operate with the officials, and please be patient, they are way more stressed than us, we need to go through this process just once per dose. Overall, it was totally worth 40 minutes of my travel to this centre.

featured_reviews.name: Naseem Shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text:
Outside India currently and had my wife visit her clinic as she is currently pregnant. She had the most disturbing experience speaking with Dr. Vaishali Ghiya, the primary obstetrician at Carewel.

We had first visited Carewel 3 years ago for our first child. For the delivery, however, I had to take my wife to the hospital at 3 AM and there was no transport available. So we decided to go to the second hospital that we had registered in which was closer to where we live.

My wife had the Carewel file from her previous pregnancy which she carried  with her yesterday while visiting Carewel hospital. Dr Vaishali Ghiya was clearly upset that we chose to go to the second hospital on our list last time.

She made so many nasty comments that my wife almost cried. It's a shame that someone so educated has such a vile tongue. Some of the comments that she made are:

1. You guys are so poor. Maybe you cannot afford treatment here.
2. You should go to a government hospital
3. I will charge Rs 1500 to give an IV. Can you afford that? Should I start the treatment?
4. Why did you come here now? Why didn’t you go to the second hospital? Did something go wrong there?
5. Why are you coming when you are so far along?
6. There are two medicines, one for 1800, one for 2400 which one can you afford?

My wife and MIL, being kind and reserved, took these comments in silence. But is this any way for a doctor to talk to the patients? What kind of an example does it set for those working under her? Will nurses and wardboys also have the same attitude when a patient is admitted?

For perspective, my wife and I have a combined income of over 36LPA and, if we wanted, we could go to the most expensive hospital in Mumbai. We are shocked to see such an attitude from a doctor that treats women when they are at their most vulnerable. Honestly, I think we dodged a bullet here.

The irony is that my modestly dressed wife and I could pay for 12 deliveries at Carewel and still have money left over from our monthly income.

featured_reviews.name: Saiesh Chodankar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Dr. Minakshi is an exceptional doctor who provided outstanding care for my wife during her pregnancy. We received her number from my cousin who delivered at her hospital and highly recommended us to speak with Dr. Minakshi. As we are based out of London, we did not have the opportunity to meet her in person. However, despite this, Dr. Minakshi has been incredibly supportive, friendly, and helpful. She even gave us her personal number to accommodate the time difference between our locations.

Throughout the entire pregnancy, Dr. Minakshi has been available to answer all of our questions and concerns, providing us with expert advice and recommendations for medications. She was always prompt and her availability helped to put our minds at ease at every step of the way.

What truly stands out about Dr. Minakshi is her unwavering commitment to her patients. Despite providing such exceptional care, she never once requested any fees from us, showing her genuine concern for our well-being and not just the financial aspect of her practice.

Overall, I recommend Dr. Minakshi highly enough. She is a truly remarkable doctor who has made a significant impact on our lives, even though we did not have the opportunity to meet her in person. We are grateful to have had such a compassionate and skilled physician caring for us during this special time in our lives.
